Well, here's what I did in what became my Near Mint:

Round 1

Voss: Ion-Lancer targets Wraith, Shock Infantry targets Bunker

Tempest: Chain Lightning (4 -> TCF Conqueror, 3 -> Frosthound, 2 -> Ion-Lancer), skip power

Wraith: Razor Ordnance Psi-Weaver

Tachyon: Nimble Strike

Bunker: External Combustion, skip power

Absolute Zero: Isothermic Transducer, Elemental Wrath Infantry

Round 2

Voss: Both of Zero's reactions on Targeting Innocents

Tempest: Shielding Winds, Sacrifice

Wraith: Smoke Bombs, Razor Ordnance TCF Conqueror

Tachyon: Fleet of Foot, HUD Goggles, Research Grant, Team Leader

Bunker: Adhesive Foam Grenade, skip power

Absolute Zero: Coolant Blast Targeting Innocents

Megalopolis: Target Absolute Zero first, reaction damage on Targeting Innocents

Round 3

Voss: Destroy Research Grant, Conqueror hits Tempest first, Zero second, reaction damage on TCF Conqueror, Shock Infantry targets Wraith, Soldier targets Tempest

Tempest: Cleansing Downpour, Cleansing Downpour

Wraith: Micro-Targeting Computer, Razor Ordnance Infantry

Tachyon: Quick Insight, discard Accelerated Assault & Sucker Punch, Fleet of Foot, Nimble Strike

Bunker: Recharge Mode

Absolute Zero: Onboard Module Installation x3 (Null-Point, Isothermic, Null-Point), Focused Apertures, Coolant Blast TCF Conqueror

With Conqueror and Targeting Innocents gone and Cleansing Downpour out, you can steadily regain HP while getting your team setup. Don't flip Voss until you're ready to take him out in a round or two; double card plays sucks tremendously if you're not ready for it.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
With the help of Dolphin's excellent opener, and the general advice of the others here, I finally managed to beat it. 

Once the ship was down and people were a bit more set up, the fight felt a LOT more equal. I focused on healing with Tempest, bolstered by one-shots for direct damage and some control.

Wraith scouted for forced deployments and kept surprises to a minimum (and did damage where surprise was unavoidable). 

Tach kept everyone in cards, destroyed pesky monorails, hypersoniced, and generally was a jack of all trades.

Bunker tanked with Smoke Bombs and Plating, doing a lot of grenade launching and combusting when a Forced Deployment brought out minions. 

AZ did a lot of Isothermic retribution in the early game, and in the mid to late game did a lot of cleaning up stragglers and focusing on Voss.

I wished I'd been a bit more careful about SubZero atmosphere though- there were a couple of turns where a Voss's end (start of turn) card play brought out a deployment, which then popped and brought out all minions, who then all went.  Given that he had only a few cards left and I'd been relentlessly putting the Deployments at the bottom of the deck, it shouldn't have been such a surprise!  Still, we weathered the onslaught and managed to take them all out... and prepare better for the next time. 

I'm glad I finally beat it. I've got some new respect for Advanced Voss... and a bit more for F6 Tempest as well.

posts.cooked:
Managed to get Mint, but I really shouldn’t have!
I knew when I saw it was this team that I should have done some big card draw but I decided to go another route. I left the ship and Targeting Innocents out and applied shenanigans with a first round Smoke Bombs to both mitigate damage and direct as much flame as possible to Absolute Zero who had used his Transducer. On round two AZ placed and used Coolant Blast to destroy the ship, and unfortunately that was about the sum of his damage-dealing. Soon after, he seemed to forget about the Cramped Quarters and punched himself to death.
The rest of the game went like so:
Tempest killed one or two things per turn and used Cleansing Downpour. Never used his innate power once. He saved Into the Stratosphere for the Forced Deployments so only one of those actually went off.
Wraith focused on damage, using Throwing Knives and Razor Ordinance every turn. When Tempest put the first Forced Deployment back, Wraith used the Eyepiece (one turn too late, because the other top card was also Forced Deployment.)
Tachy Sucker-Punched those pesky Soldiers that were immune to projectile and threw cards at everyone. She also shut down damage twice, and very timely.
Bunker dealt and soaked damage. A lot of damage. No Omni-cannon for me, but Turret Mode with Flak Cannon + Grenade Launcher with the occasional Maintenance.
Incapsolute Zero shut down the environment because that’s what he does.
With the final card (the first Forced Deployment back for a third time) of Voss’s deck imminent and everyone under 5hp Bunker and Tempest cleared the table so Wraith could sacrifice her tech and Tachion could double Barrage for 49 points between them.

And right before that the game glitched (see attached.) It’s actually the second time I saw this happen in a game, and on that character’s turn they didn’t actually have the card. Fun though

…and the villain/environment deck were stacked to make the fight harder than it should have been.  Two Hostage Situations in the first five rounds?  C'mon!  I played this same scenario as a custom game (i.e. picking Advanced Voss/Freedom Five/Megalopolis) five times after finishing the one-shot, and wiped the floor with Advanced Voss every time.  

 

AZ is the key–once he has his two modules, you make sure he's the highest HP hero, then kill all of the minions except the one that does 2 fire damage to the highest HP hero.  Now you're essentially immune to damage from Voss, because the minion will whack AZ for 2 fire damage…which AZ will redirect into cold damage aimed at himself, thus healing himself from the fire damage.  From that point, you're free to build your hands/setups (using the insane amounts of card draw these heroes have) and kill Voss at your leisure.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Mint, and definitely a slow-burn game. Voss was down to 5 cards in his deck by the time I was finished, Wraith's deck and trash were both empty and my computer nearly froze when I was picking out which cards to load the Omni-Cannon with. Absolute Zero was MVP, as I'm getting is expected with this one, and this is the first game I got real mileage out of Coolant Blast.

I actually really liked having a long game -- most games I have are over quick enough that AZ only manages to get out his basic equipment, and it was nice to have more of his stuff out for longer.

Both the Forced Deployments I saw came out with Voss flipped, which made them easy to deal with (one set fell to Grappling Hook, Razor Ordnance to deal with the Gene-Bound Guard, and a Sonic Vortex to wipe out everyone else; the second went down to a Fueled Freeze, with a pair of Synaptic Interruptions going down to boost it to 3+Focused Apertures).
